texts.li: {X_nameDef} came in with the {FACTION} party as a carrier, and has spent two days working up the nerve. Tonight {X_nameDef} caught {A_nameDef} by the woodpile and told {A_objective} about a debt that grows faster than anyone could pay it. {X_nameDef} will not walk home with them if there is any other way.\n\n"On the road they say you don't turn people away here," {X_nameDef} said. "They say you even feed your prisoners." {FACTION} will not thank the colony for keeping what it considers its own.

{X_nameDef} has a split lip and a story to go with it. {X_nameDef} didn't come with the {FACTION} party by choice, and wants to stay behind when they leave. {X_nameDef} came to {A_nameDef} because, as {X_pronoun} put it, people between here and the river say this is the place that spares people.\n\nWhoever leads the {FACTION} group has seen {X_nameDef} talking to colonists, and has kept a close eye on {X_objective} since.

At the well this morning, {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} under {X_possessive} breath whether the colony would hide {X_objective} from {X_possessive} own people. {FACTION} has no use for {X_nameDef} beyond the work, and the work is killing {X_objective}.\n\n"I heard you're merciful here," {X_nameDef} said, watching {A_nameDef}'s face.

li.label: Take {X_objective} in
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} slept inside the walls that night and has joined the colony. The {FACTION} party left at dawn one carrier short, and its leader made it plain this would be remembered.

li.label: Tell {FACTION} what {X_nameDef} asked
li.outcome: The council told the {FACTION} leader what {X_nameDef} had asked. {X_nameDef} left with them in the morning, walking at the front, where someone could keep an eye on {X_objective}. People on the road will hear about this one too.

li.label: A night's rest, then the road
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} got a warm corner, a full bowl and a night's sleep without anyone shouting at {X_objective}. In the morning {X_nameDef} left with {FACTION}, with a loaf of the colony's bread in {X_possessive} pack.

texts.li: {X_nameDef} has heard what travelers say about the colony, that it lets its prisoners go, and is acting like it. {X_nameDef} lies on the cell bed with {X_possessive} feet up, sends back the porridge, and tells {A_nameDef} through the bars to hurry up with the release.\n\n{A_nameDef} is tired of being laughed at by a prisoner, and has asked the council what the colony's mercy is actually for.

"You lot let everybody go," {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} this morning, cheerfully, through the cell door. "Might as well do it now and save the bread." {X_nameDef} has said some version of this every day since the capture, and some of the wardens have started to wonder whether {X_nameDef} is right.\n\n{A_nameDef} wants the council to settle whether the colony's mercy is a promise or a choice.

li.label: Show {X_objective} the colony's other side
li.outcome: The watch on {X_nameDef}'s cell was doubled, the extra blanket taken away, and the wardens stopped answering {X_possessive} jokes. {X_nameDef} has gone quiet, and {A_nameDef} is pleased about it.

li.label: Let {X_objective} go, then
li.outcome: The wardens have orders to release {X_nameDef}, who grinned at them all the way to the door. Word will get around that the stories are true.

li.label: Treat {X_objective} like any other prisoner
li.outcome: Nothing changes. {X_nameDef} is fed, watched and spoken to like any other prisoner, and the release {X_pronoun} keeps asking about hasn't come. The jokes have started to dry up.

texts.li: The last caravan brought back what people say about the colony on the roads. In the villages of {FACTION}, mothers use its name to get their children indoors before dark. {A_nameDef} heard it and has been troubled ever since.\n\n{FACTION} has had a hard season, with fever in the villages and not enough to eat. {A_nameDef} has asked the council to send them food and ask nothing for it, so that the next story told about this place is a different one.

{A_nameDef} has never liked what the colony is known for, and this week a trader said it to {A_possessive} face: hard people behind hard walls, who give nothing and spare no one. {A_nameDef} wants the council to do one merciful thing that people will hear about.\n\n{FACTION} is short of food after a bad harvest. {A_nameDef} thinks a few sacks of grain, sent with no price attached, would be talked about from one village to the next.

{A_nameDef} found a child of {FACTION} hiding behind the woodpile, too frightened to come out. The child had heard what this colony does to strangers. {A_nameDef} walked the child back to the road, then came straight to the council.\n\nThe child's people are hungry this year. "Send them food," {A_nameDef} said. "Once. Let one of them grow up telling a different story about us."

li.label: Send food, and ask nothing
li.outcome: Sacks of the colony's food went out the gate for {FACTION}, with no letter and no price. {A_nameDef} helped load them, and seemed lighter for it.

li.label: Send silver instead
li.outcome: Eighty silver went to {FACTION} with a passing caravan. It will buy them bread. {A_nameDef} would rather it had been food from the colony's own stores.

li.label: Let them talk
li.outcome: The council decided a name that frightens people is worth keeping. {A_nameDef} left the meeting without a word.

texts.li: The {FACTION} party has brought one of its own before the council. {X_nameDef} was caught with a hand in the caravan's purse. They could punish {X_objective} themselves, but they would rather the colony did it: this colony has a name for not flinching, and no one will blame their leader for what happens here.\n\nThey have asked for {A_nameDef} by name to hold the whip. {X_nameDef} is standing in the yard with {X_possessive} hands tied, looking at the ground.

{X_nameDef} stole from {X_possessive} own caravan, and the {FACTION} leader wants it punished properly, by people with a name for it. "We heard how you do things," the leader told the council, and nodded at {A_nameDef}.\n\n{X_nameDef} hasn't said a word since being dragged in. {A_nameDef} hasn't either.

li.label: Flog {X_objective}
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} did it in the yard, in front of both peoples. The {FACTION} leader thanked the council. {X_nameDef} walked out with the caravan in the morning, stiffly, and didn't look back.

li.label: Pardon {X_objective}
li.outcome: The council pardoned {X_nameDef} and untied {X_possessive} hands. The {FACTION} leader spat in the dirt and walked off. Before the caravan left, {X_nameDef} came back to the gate to thank the council.

li.label: Not our thief, not our business
li.outcome: The council said it judges its own people, not other people's. The {FACTION} leader dealt with {X_nameDef} outside the walls, and the council didn't ask how.

texts.li: Word has spread that there's always a bowl at this colony's gate. Hungry people from {FACTION} have come four times this month, more of them each time, and some bring cousins.\n\n{A_nameDef} has been feeding them, and has brought the storeroom tally to the council. The colony can keep giving for a while, but not forever.

Another knock at the gate, another thin face from {FACTION} and a story about a burned granary or a lame ox. {A_nameDef}, who does the cooking and most of the counting, has started hiding the good bread.\n\n"It's not that I mind," {A_nameDef} told the council. "It's that it's every day now. And the cold months are still coming."

{A_nameDef} counted the bowls handed out at the gate this season and stopped at sixty. Word on the road is that the colony never says no, and {FACTION} has clearly heard it.\n\nThe storeroom isn't empty yet. {A_nameDef} wants the council to decide how much more goes out before it is.

li.label: Keep the gate open and the pot full
li.outcome: The gate stays open to anyone who comes hungry. Another week's worth of food went out of the storeroom, {FACTION} speaks warmly of the colony, and {A_nameDef} has started cooking in bigger pots.

li.label: Food for work
li.outcome: From now on, anyone who comes for a bowl splits wood for it first. Most of them do, and the woodpile is thirty logs higher. A few of the hungry have stopped coming.

li.label: Close the gate to beggars
li.outcome: The next hungry family from {FACTION} was sent on with nothing, and so was the one after that. The storeroom will last the winter. Travelers will have something new to say about the colony.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, the {FACTION} trader, weighed {A_nameDef}'s silver twice, bit a coin, and asked loudly whether the colony charged guests for the well water too. "Word is you lot count every grain," {X_nameDef} said. "Thought I'd save you the bother."\n\nThe caravan guards laughed. {A_nameDef} went red to the ears, and wants the council to answer it one way or another.

{X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has heard the colony is tight with its silver, and keeps making jokes about it: mice starving in the storeroom, guests charged for well water. {A_nameDef} laughed the first time.\n\nBy the fifth time {A_nameDef} had stopped laughing, and has asked the council to do something to shut {X_nameDef} up. A gift, perhaps, that no one could call mean.

li.label: Send {X_nameDef} off with a gift
li.outcome: The council gave {X_nameDef} fifty silver "for the road", in front of the caravan guards. {X_nameDef} looked at the purse for a long moment and made no more jokes that evening.

li.label: Let {X_objective} laugh
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} kept up the jokes until the caravan left, and {A_nameDef} stayed in {A_possessive} room until it was out of sight.

li.label: Charge {X_objective} for the well water, then
li.outcome: The council took the joke and made it policy: {X_nameDef}'s pack animals drank at two silver a bucket, twenty silver in all. {X_nameDef} paid and left in a temper. {A_nameDef} wishes {A_pronoun} had never brought it up.

texts.li: Supper here follows old rules. No one eats until everyone is seated, no one leaves before the last bowl is scraped, and a full bowl is set at the head of the table for the dead. {A_nameDef} has started eating standing up by the kitchen door, and called the bowl for the dead a waste of good stew where {B_nameDef} could hear.\n\n{B_nameDef} has brought it to the council. {A_nameDef} says it's only a bowl of stew. {B_nameDef} says the bowl is for the people buried out back, and {A_nameDef} knows it.

When the season turns, the colony gathers at the graves at dusk and says the names of the dead. The custom is older than most of the walls. {A_nameDef} skipped it last time to finish a job, and has said {A_pronoun} will skip it again, since the dead won't notice and the work will.\n\n{B_nameDef} is angry about it, and has asked the council to remind {A_nameDef} what kind of place this is.

Every newcomer to this colony is met at the gate with bread and salt, and all hands turn out for it. {A_nameDef} didn't come down for the last one, and told {B_nameDef} afterward that standing in a line holding bread is theater, not work.\n\n{B_nameDef} has asked the council to settle it. Either the customs here are kept, {B_nameDef} says, or there's no point in having them.

li.label: The custom stands, for everyone
li.outcome: The council ruled that the custom stands, for everyone, every time. {A_nameDef} turned up the next time and went through it with a sour face. {B_nameDef} says that will do for now.

li.label: Let {A_nameDef} choose
li.outcome: The council said a custom kept under orders isn't worth much, and left it to {A_nameDef}. {B_nameDef} took the ruling hard, and has been keeping the custom more carefully than ever.

li.label: Have {B_nameDef} tell {A_objective} why it matters
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} sat {A_nameDef} down and told {A_objective} who the custom was for and how it started. {A_nameDef} came out quieter, and was there the next time, on time.
li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef} sat {A_nameDef} down to explain the custom. Ten minutes in, {A_nameDef} called it superstition, {B_nameDef} called {A_nameDef} something worse, and the two of them had to be pulled apart.

texts.li: When the first frost came, the colony used to eat together at one long table. Somebody sang badly, and someone told the story of how the place was founded. Between the new kiln, the new fields and every other new project, it stopped happening.\n\n{A_nameDef} wants it back. The others aren't against it. They're just busy with whatever comes next.

The fields go in new rows every season and the kitchen changes its bread every week. Somewhere along the way, the evenings when each person told one story stopped happening.\n\n{A_nameDef} has asked the council to bring those evenings back, and to keep them this time. "We can try new things," {A_nameDef} said. "We could also keep one old one."

Travelers call this the colony that never sits still, and {A_nameDef} is tired of it. There used to be a harvest supper here, with one long table and a toast to the first people who broke this ground. Ask around and people disagree about when the last one was.\n\n{A_nameDef} has asked the council to bring it back.

li.label: Bring it back, the way it was
li.outcome: The old custom came back as {A_nameDef} remembered it, bad singing included. People stayed at the table long after the food was gone.

li.label: Bring it back, with a few changes
li.outcome: The old custom is back with changes: the same table, new songs, and a different dish each time. {A_nameDef} says it isn't how it was, but hasn't missed one yet.

li.label: Let the old ways rest
li.outcome: The council said the colony has outgrown it. {A_nameDef} didn't argue, but left supper early that night and went to bed without a word.

texts.li: The colony's gate is always open, and {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has made the most of it. In two days {X_nameDef} has eaten at every table, borrowed {A_nameDef}'s good cloak without asking, and twice been found asleep in {A_nameDef}'s bed.\n\n{A_nameDef} isn't angry, exactly, but has asked the council where a welcome is supposed to end.

{X_nameDef} came in with the {FACTION} visitors and no longer acts like a visitor. {X_nameDef} gives the cook advice, tells the haulers where to put things, and has started calling the storeroom "ours." Yesterday {A_nameDef} came back from the fields to find {X_nameDef} rearranging {A_possessive} workbench.\n\nThe colony is known for its welcome. {A_nameDef} would like to know how far it goes.

Travelers say a stranger is always welcome here, and {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has taken them at their word. {X_nameDef} has drunk most of a cask, borrowed {A_nameDef}'s boots, and given a long speech at supper about how the colony ought to be run.\n\n{A_nameDef} has asked the council, politely, whether there's a limit.

li.label: Guests are guests
li.outcome: The council said a welcome with conditions isn't much of a welcome. {X_nameDef} carried on as before, and {A_nameDef} has started locking {A_possessive} things away.

li.label: Put {X_objective} to work
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} was handed an axe and told that guests who live like family can work like family. {X_nameDef} grumbled, but split a good pile of wood before supper and slept in {X_possessive} own bedroll that night.
li.riskOutcome: {X_nameDef} was handed an axe, dropped it at {A_nameDef}'s feet, and told the yard at length what {X_pronoun} thought of hosts who make their guests chop wood. The {FACTION} visitors are packing up to leave early, and they're angry about it.

li.label: Ask the {FACTION} visitors to move on
li.outcome: The council thanked the {FACTION} party for its visit and asked them to be on their way by noon. {X_nameDef} complained all the way to the gate, and {A_nameDef} changed the sheets.

texts.li: {X_nameDef} came with the {FACTION} party, and {A_nameDef} knew {X_objective} on sight. They grew up together, a long time ago and a long way from here. The gate watch kept {X_nameDef} outside the walls with the pack animals, as the colony does with every stranger now.\n\n{A_nameDef} has asked the council to let {X_objective} in for supper, just this once.

{X_nameDef}, one of the {FACTION} visitors, once shared a cell, a boat and most of a bad winter with {A_nameDef}, long before the colony. Tonight {X_nameDef} is sleeping outside the walls, because the colony doesn't let outsiders in after dark.\n\n{A_nameDef} has never asked the council for a favor before, and is asking for one now.

The colony's gate stays shut to strangers, and every trader on the road knows it. Tonight one of the strangers outside it is {X_nameDef}, who {A_nameDef} says is the closest thing to family {A_pronoun} has left.\n\n{A_nameDef} is standing at the gate and has sent word to the council: open it, or {A_nameDef} will spend the night out there too.

li.label: Open the gate for {X_objective}
li.outcome: The gate opened for {X_nameDef}, who ate at the colony's table next to {A_nameDef} and talked late into the night about people from before. In the morning the watch checked the storeroom twice. Nothing was missing.

li.label: The rule is the rule
li.outcome: The gate stayed shut. {A_nameDef} passed a bowl of stew and a blanket over the wall, and in the morning {X_nameDef} passed back the bowl, empty.

li.label: {A_nameDef} can go out to {X_objective}
li.outcome: The gate stayed shut, but {A_nameDef} went out through it with a lantern, a jug and two cups. The two of them sat by {X_nameDef}'s fire until it burned down, and the watch on the wall could hear them laughing.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} fell asleep on {A_possessive} feet at the threshing floor this morning and went down hard. This colony is known for working from before sunrise to after dark, and for being proud of it.\n\n{A_nameDef} has asked the council for one day off. Not a sick day, just a day to sit somewhere and do nothing, without anyone keeping count.

The colony has a name for hard work, and {A_nameDef} has worked harder than most. It shows in {A_possessive} shaking hands and short temper, and this week {A_nameDef} dropped a full bucket down the well and just stood there staring after it.\n\n{A_nameDef} came to the council and asked, barely above a whisper, whether anyone here is ever allowed a day of rest.

Traders say this colony works dark to dark, and they mean it as praise. {A_nameDef} has been working dark to dark for a season, and has started to hear it differently.\n\n"One day," {A_nameDef} told the council. "I'm not asking for a week. I'm asking for one day where nobody needs me for anything."

li.label: Give {A_objective} the day
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} has a few easy days, by order of the council. On the first, {A_nameDef} sat by the water from breakfast to supper, did nothing useful at all, and came in looking rested for once.

li.label: A day of rest for everyone
li.outcome: The council declared a day of rest for the whole colony. People wandered about in the morning, unsure what to do with themselves. By afternoon they were lying in the grass, arguing about the shapes of clouds.

li.label: The work won't wait
li.outcome: The council said the work won't wait. {A_nameDef} nodded, went back out, and did it, slower than before.
li.riskOutcome: The council said the work won't wait. {A_nameDef} went back out, put the tools down halfway across the yard, and walked off toward the trees. Somebody will have to go after {A_objective}.

texts.li: This colony is known for taking its time, and most people here are happy to live up to it. {A_nameDef} has been bringing in the crops more or less alone while the others nap in the shade, and today threw a sickle down in the middle of the yard.\n\n"I'm not carrying all of you through another winter," {A_nameDef} told the council. Several people looked up from their naps to listen.

Visitors envy the colony's easy pace. {A_nameDef} has stopped finding it charming. The fields are {A_nameDef}'s, most of the hauling is {A_nameDef}'s, and this morning {A_nameDef} found the woodpile empty and three colonists asleep against it.\n\n{A_nameDef} wants the council to make everyone pull their weight, or at least to say out loud who's been pulling it.

{A_nameDef} counted. Of everything sown and brought in this season, most went through {A_nameDef}'s hands, and the colony's long lunches got longer the whole time.\n\n"I don't mind work," {A_nameDef} told the council. "I mind being the only one doing it."

li.label: Everyone pulls their weight
li.outcome: Chores were handed out by name and posted by the kitchen door. The naps got shorter and the grumbling got louder, and {A_nameDef} finally got a full night's sleep.

li.label: Thank {A_nameDef} at supper
li.outcome: The council stood up at supper and thanked {A_nameDef} by name for the season's harvest. {A_nameDef} turned red, said it was nothing, and was back in the fields at dawn in better spirits.

li.label: Tell {A_objective} to slow down too
li.outcome: The council told {A_nameDef} the work would still be there tomorrow. {A_nameDef} said that was what worried {A_objective}, but took a few days in the shade anyway, scowling at the fields.
